spec.goal: POST /items rejects a name longer than 64 characters with HTTP 400 and body { "error": "name too long" }, while accepting a name of exactly 64 characters with the existing 201 create behavior. "Longer than 64" is measured as JavaScript String.length (UTF-16 code units) on the raw request value, with no trimming or normalization. The length check runs only after the existing presence/type check in toy/src/app.js, so the current missing-name / non-string / empty-string 400 { "error": "name is required" } responses are unchanged. No other route, field, or response shape changes.

acceptance.given: a running app instance with an empty item store
acceptance.when: a client sends POST /items with content-type application/json and body { "name": <a 65-character string> }
acceptance.then: the response status is 400, the JSON body deep-equals { "error": "name too long" }, and a subsequent GET /items returns [] (the item was not created)

acceptance.given: a running app instance with an empty item store
acceptance.when: a client sends POST /items with body { "name": <a string of exactly 64 characters> }
acceptance.then: the response status is 201, the JSON body is { id: <number>, name: <the same 64-character string> }, and a subsequent GET /items returns exactly that one item

acceptance.given: a running app instance with an empty item store
acceptance.when: a client sends POST /items with body { "name": <a string of exactly 63 characters> }
acceptance.then: the response status is 201 and the created item's name equals the 63-character string, confirming the boundary rejects only lengths strictly greater than 64

acceptance.when: a client sends POST /items with body {} (no name field)
acceptance.then: the response status is 400 and the JSON body deep-equals { "error": "name is required" }, unchanged from current behavior

acceptance.when: a client sends POST /items with body { "name": "" } (empty string) and, separately, { "name": 123 } (non-string)
acceptance.then: in both cases the response status is 400 and the JSON body deep-equals { "error": "name is required" }; the new length check never turns these into "name too long"

acceptance.given: a running app instance with an empty item store and a name of 200 characters (well past the limit)
acceptance.when: a client sends POST /items with that 200-character name and then sends POST /items with { "name": "widget" }
acceptance.then: the first response is 400 { "error": "name too long" }, the second is 201, and the created item's id is 1 — a rejected over-length request consumes no id and mutates no state

acceptance.when: `npm test` is run from the toy/ directory
acceptance.then: every pre-existing test in toy/test/items.test.js and toy/test/health.test.js still passes alongside the new length-limit tests, and the run exits 0

out_of_scope: Any change to GET /items, GET /health, or GET /items/:id (the latter belongs to wi-1 — do not add or modify that route here).
Changing the existing missing-name / non-string / empty-string error message, status, or check ordering; 'name is required' stays exactly as it is and is still evaluated first.
Trimming, whitespace collapsing, Unicode normalization (NFC/NFD), grapheme-cluster counting, or byte-length counting — the limit is raw String.length in UTF-16 code units.
Making the 64-character limit configurable via env var, config file, or request parameter; the constant is hard-coded in toy/src/app.js.
Adding a minimum-length rule, character-set validation, content/profanity filtering, or duplicate-name rejection.
Validating or limiting any field other than `name`, and rejecting requests that carry extra unknown fields.
Introducing a validation library (zod, joi, express-validator) or a shared validation middleware layer; the check stays inline in the existing route handler.
Changing the error response envelope shape (e.g. adding `code`, `field`, or `details` keys) for this or any other error.
Truncating an over-length name and accepting it instead of rejecting it.
Request body size limits, rate limiting, auth, or any other request-level middleware.
Persistence beyond the existing in-memory Map, and any change to id allocation strategy.
toy/README.md, OpenAPI/schema docs, or CHANGELOG updates.
risk_reasons: Touches public API: modifies POST /items endpoint behavior, affecting all external consumers
Breaks backward compatibility: requests with names > 64 characters change from 201 to 400, impacting existing clients
Affects external contract: changes the validation rules exposed to API consumers

tasks.description: Implement POST /items name length validation: add a check in the route handler that rejects names longer than 64 UTF-16 code units with HTTP 400 { "error": "name too long" }, accepting exactly 64 or shorter with existing 201 create behavior. The check must run after the existing presence/type validation so existing error messages remain unchanged.

decision.note: Delegated by HE in chat: enforce the 64-char limit as specified; no external consumers, so the router's compatibility concern does not apply.
